references.text: Ehud also gathered the men of Ephraim to seize the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, a similar military strategy that Gideon used.
Jephthah used the same strategy by taking control of the fords of the Jordan to prevent the Ephraimites from fleeing.
Earlier in Gideon's story, he also sent messengers to gather men from several tribes, including Ephraim.
The men of Ephraim complained that they were called late to battle, referring to this event in chapter 7.
The hill country of Ephraim is mentioned as a significant geographical area, the same region where Gideon sent messengers.
Beth-Barah is mentioned in connection with the Jordan area, the same place as in Gideon's strategy.
Water sources and the fords across the Jordan were of strategic importance throughout biblical history.
